newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek foreign minister to visit Milosevic on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Greek foreign minister to visit Milosevic on Sunday.

text.p: Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos will go to Belgrade on Sunday to meet Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic as well as opposition party leaders who have led protests against his rule for almost two months.
The foreign ministry said the meetings had not been fixed as yet but were expected to be during the day. Pangalos also hopes to meet Patriarch Pavle of the Serbian Orthodox Church.
Diplomatic sources said Pangalos's visit was aimed at easing tensions between Milosevic and the opposition parties.
Opposition parties have demonstrated for the past 53 days against the cancellation of municipal election results by Milosevic's ruling Socialists last November.
After ethnic wars erupted in June 1990 and ravaged former Yugoslavia, Greece maintained close ties with Milosevic while its Western allies branded him the instigator of the conflicts.
But since the Greek socialist party won elections in late 1993, Athens has kept a more distant, low-key stance towards him.
